children: By George Glover and Nate Wolf

A wild few weeks for the artificial-intelligence trade haven't deterred Anthropic from pushing ahead with its trillion-dollar initial public offering that will establish it as the market's AI bellwether.
The Claude developer said in a filing on Tuesday that it and some of its investors would sell 825 million shares of Class A stock at an estimated IPO price of between $70 and $78 a share.

At the top of that range, Anthropic would raise about $64.4 billion from its IPO. It's bidding to raise another $26 billion by selling shares to large-cap tech companies including Google, Microsoft, and Nvidia.

The private placement reads like a who's who of AI companies — Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Micron, and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. are the other companies taking part in the offering. All seven stocks were sliding on Tuesday after consumer price inflation data came in hotter than expected.

With about 13.1 billion shares outstanding, that means Anthropic is aiming for a market value of around $1.02 trillion. Its fully diluted valuation could top $1.4 trillion when accounting for the likes of options and unvested stock awards.
The big number matters most for the market. Just a couple of months ago, Anthropic was rumored to be eyeing a $2 trillion valuation — a figure Barron's called a "risky bet."

The AI trade has gone sour since then, with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei playing a role when he called for a deceleration in model development. The backlash against data centers and the scandal engulfing Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang have also rocked AI stocks.

Many on Wall Street will be happy to see Amodei push ahead with the IPO rather than waiting for conditions to improve. Delaying the listing would only sow more panic when investors appear to be getting over the worst of their AI fears. The Nasdaq jumped 2.7% on Monday.

The AI trade requires Anthropic to get the financing it needs, Jim Lebenthal, chief markets strategist at Cerity Partners, told Barron's last week. Anthropic sits at the core of the industry, with nearly $900 billion in disclosed chip and compute commitments. Getting money in the door will make counterparties and investors more comfortable about Anthropic's ability to pay.

A $1.4 trillion valuation would also provide a more attractive entry point for early investors than the $2 trillion floated earlier this year. Analysts at William Blair estimate the company will bring in $135 billion of revenue in 2027. At that level, Anthropic would trade between 10 and 11 times projected 2027 sales.

"This is an attractive multiple for a once-in-a-generation company like Anthropic operating in a technological shift that takes place once every few decades at best," wrote Arjun Bhatia, an analyst at William Blair.
Anthropic has applied to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT. The final IPO share price is expected on Nov. 18, with shares expected to begin publicly trading on Nov. 19.
